name: TinyZKP ROI and Business Case
summary: Business-case worksheet for evaluating TinyZKP proof receipts against manual replay, evidence review, support work, and self-hosted prover operations.
primary_question: Does one proof-receipt workflow avoid enough recurring review, replay, support, infrastructure, or sales friction to justify the smallest paid route?

value_drivers.name: Manual replay reduction
value_drivers.description: Reviewers can verify the encoded transition without asking engineering to reconstruct state, export logs, or explain an agent transcript.
value_drivers.evidence: Monthly review hours avoided and one receipt/verifier artifact.

value_drivers.name: Support and evidence reduction
value_drivers.description: Customers, auditors, and internal reviewers can inspect a receipt URL instead of opening repeat evidence requests.
value_drivers.evidence: Support tickets, audit requests, or customer success workflows that a receipt could satisfy.

value_drivers.name: Prover operations avoidance
value_drivers.description: TinyZKP hosted receipts and Compute avoid high-RAM workers, custom queues, verifier packaging, monitoring, and proof-format compatibility work before product fit is proven.
value_drivers.evidence: Self-hosted prover infrastructure estimate and monthly prover-ops hours avoided.

value_drivers.name: Commercial trust acceleration
value_drivers.description: Receipt-backed agent and API workflows can shorten sales, procurement, and trust review by giving buyers a portable evidence artifact.
value_drivers.evidence: Customer-visible receipt placement, trust packet, and internal buying decision.

worksheet_inputs.label: Manual review hours per month avoided
Support or evidence hours per month avoided
Prover or integration operations hours per month avoided

formula.tinyzkp_monthly_cost: plan_base + receipts_per_month * rate_for_route_and_trace_band, capped when the selected plan has a published cap

sample_cases.name: Customer-visible API mutation
sample_cases.why_it_pays: Receipts reduce support and customer evidence requests after important state-changing API calls.

sample_cases.name: Agent platform receipt policy
sample_cases.route: $5,000 pilot then platform rollout from $499/month plus usage
sample_cases.why_it_pays: Receipts become a native platform trust feature for high-value tool categories.

sample_cases.name: Long supported state-transition trace
sample_cases.why_it_pays: Trace-step pricing avoids high-RAM prover workers, custom queues, and on-call ownership for sporadic large proofs.

sample_cases.name: Audit or reserve checkpoint
sample_cases.route: Pro, Scale, Compute, or pilot depending on trace size and visibility
sample_cases.why_it_pays: Portable receipts reduce repeated audit exports and replay requests.

recommended_routes.trigger: Positive ROI with a live supported workflow
recommended_routes.route: Start with the smallest self-serve plan that supports the expected volume.

recommended_routes.trigger: Custom statement, procurement, support, or customer-visible rollout uncertainty
recommended_routes.route: Use the $5,000 production pilot before committing to annual, reserved-capacity, or platform rollout.

recommended_routes.trigger: Native agent platform or workflow-engine distribution
recommended_routes.route: Use platform rollout after one receipt-required tool category is proven.

recommended_routes.trigger: High-RAM prover operations are the primary alternative
recommended_routes.route: Use Compute or reserved capacity instead of self-hosting before demand is steady.

guardrails: Do not count value from claims the receipt does not encode.
Do not model generic private-input, zkVM, zkML, or on-chain verifier claims as live value unless the workflow has an explicit supported path.
Do not use proof receipts for low-value events where no recipient will inspect the proof.
Treat the worksheet as planning guidance; finance teams should replace defaults with internal cost data.
